parts.title: Passage 1 · Emergency Fire Procedures
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: 'Detect' means discover or notice something, which can happen through sight or hearing. Both senses can alert someone to a fire.
questions.evidence: If you detect a fire

questions.explanation: To activate an alarm is to bring it into operation or use. It does not mean run towards it or shake it.
questions.evidence: activate the nearest emergency alarm

questions.explanation: 'Proceed to' means move or go forward to a place. Here that place is the nearest exit.
questions.evidence: proceed to the exit nearest to you

questions.explanation: Vents are openings through which air or smoke can pass. The notice groups them with the space under the door.
questions.evidence: Block all openings, such as vents and under the door

questions.explanation: The notice specifically says not to use elevators. The other choices relate to actions included in its fire procedures.
questions.evidence: Do not try to exit by use of the elevators.

questions.explanation: According to the notice, after deciding it is safe to leave, the guest should proceed to the nearest exit.
questions.evidence: proceed to the exit nearest to you

questions.explanation: The notice tells guests who cannot leave safely to inform hotel staff where they are.
questions.evidence: Call the hotel staff, informing them of your location.

questions.explanation: The notice says to cover the mouth with a wet towel if smoke is already in the room. This answer uses the permitted three words.
questions.evidence: hold a wet towel over your mouth

questions.explanation: The notice warns against breaking windows unless it is absolutely necessary.
questions.evidence: Do not break any windows unless absolutely necessary.

questions.explanation: The final paragraph identifies staying calm during evacuation as the key to success.
questions.evidence: your ability to STAY CALM during the evacuation process is the key to success

parts.title: Passage 2 · Out of the Wild, into Our Homes
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: An endangered species is in danger, especially of disappearing or becoming extinct.
questions.evidence: Declaring a species endangered

questions.explanation: 'Dwindling' means becoming smaller in number. The protection groups were showing that some elephant populations were falling.
questions.evidence: certain populations of elephants were dwindling

questions.explanation: To fade is to gradually become weaker or disappear. The writer describes public concern declining over time.
questions.evidence: concern for a certain species tends to fade after a while

questions.explanation: 'Clubbed' means beaten with a heavy object or club. It does not mean shot or kicked.
questions.evidence: pups being clubbed to death

questions.explanation: The second paragraph says animal parts are used for products including powders claimed to improve people's lives.
questions.evidence: People use parts of animals for everything

questions.explanation: The passage describes elephants being killed so people can obtain the ivory in their tusks.
questions.evidence: elephants with their faces sawed off for their ivory tusks

questions.explanation: After discussing elephants, the writer describes the killing of young seals in the late 1970s and again ten years later.
questions.evidence: people protested against the slaughter of seal pups

questions.explanation: The passage names tuna fishermen as the people from whom dolphins need protection.
questions.evidence: protecting dolphins from the tuna fishermen

questions.explanation: The writer explicitly says these choices are not about food, shelter or anything else humans need to survive. The cause given is greed.
questions.evidence: These choices have nothing to do with food or shelter or anything else that helps humans survive.

questions.explanation: The passage says declaring a species endangered and making laws is not always enough, which contradicts the statement.
questions.evidence: protecting it by laws is not always enough

questions.explanation: Poachers kill animals illegally, and the passage says they rarely get caught. They therefore often escape detection.
questions.evidence: Poachers, people who kill wildlife illegally, rarely get caught.

questions.explanation: The protection groups demonstrated that some elephant populations were decreasing. 'Dwindling' expresses that decrease.
questions.evidence: These groups also proved that certain populations of elephants were dwindling.

questions.explanation: The passage mentions stronger laws but gives no details about how severe the punishments are. A legal ban does not establish the level of punishment.
questions.evidence: Laws against poaching were strengthened.

questions.explanation: The late 1970s were followed by a temporary halt, but ten years later the number killed was higher than ever. That places the later increase in the late 1980s.
questions.evidence: But ten years later, the number of seal pups killed was higher than ever.

questions.explanation: The text says the whale population seems to have increased but does not give stricter laws as the cause. The laws discussed next concern dolphins.
questions.evidence: The whale population appears to have increased for now.

questions.explanation: The ending warns that attention may turn to other endangered species and asks whether elephants will then be forgotten. The statement expresses this possibility, not a certainty.
questions.evidence: the protests and the publicity will probably turn to some other endangered species

parts.title: Passage 1 · Hotel Directory of Services
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: In this exercise, laundry refers to the place where clothes are washed and ironed.
questions.evidence: laundry

questions.explanation: A lounge is a public sitting or waiting room.
questions.evidence: lounge

questions.explanation: 'Essential' means necessary or needed.
questions.evidence: essential toiletries

questions.explanation: 'Prevailing' describes the rate currently in general use.
questions.evidence: the prevailing rate

questions.explanation: A valuable is a possession worth a lot of money.
questions.evidence: Please do not leave valuables in your room.

questions.explanation: To retrieve something is to recover or get it back.
questions.evidence: you may retrieve your messages

questions.explanation: For rooms on floors 3–9, dial 7 followed by the room number. Room 408 therefore requires 7408.
questions.evidence: Room to Room, Floors 3–9: 7+Room Number

questions.explanation: The theatre and concerts entry directs guests to the concierge at 1884.
questions.evidence: THEATRE/CONCERTS — 1884

questions.explanation: The emergency entry supplies the internal hotel number for fire, police or medical help.
questions.evidence: EMERGENCY — 1999

questions.explanation: An extra pillow is an extra room supply, so the appropriate service is Housekeeping.
questions.evidence: HOUSEKEEPING — 1806

questions.explanation: For tours of the preferred business floors, including floors 11 and 12, the directory gives the Manager on Duty's extension.
questions.evidence: Contact our Manager on Duty (extension 1888).

questions.explanation: The newsstand is on the Lobby Level, so this is the listed place to obtain newspapers.
questions.evidence: NEWSSTAND — Lobby Level

questions.explanation: Overnight laundry operates Monday to Friday only, rather than every day.
questions.evidence: returned 7 a.m. next day, Monday through Friday only

questions.explanation: Half a minute is thirty seconds. The directory says calls ringing longer than this incur a charge.
questions.evidence: you will be charged the prevailing rate should your call ring more than 30 seconds

questions.explanation: The hotel's stated condition is that valuables are secured in safe deposit boxes, not simply that reception is informed about valuables left in a room.
questions.evidence: unless valuables are secured in safe deposit boxes

questions.explanation: The directory mentions self-parking next to the hotel but does not say how many cars the facility holds.
questions.evidence: Our self-parking facility is located adjacent to the hotel.

questions.explanation: Saturday dinner service ends at 10:30 p.m., so a 10:35 arrival is too late.
questions.evidence: Dinner 6 p.m.–10:30 p.m. Monday–Saturday

questions.explanation: The local-call instructions explicitly advise adding 1 after 9 if the initial dialling attempt gives a busy signal.
questions.evidence: If 9+Number results in a busy signal, call 9+1+Number.

questions.explanation: 89 is for retrieving voicemail inside the room. Calling from outside the hotel requires the full telephone number and the operator.
questions.evidence: Outside the hotel (310)645-7500. The Operator will connect you to voicemail.

questions.explanation: The security list tells guests to notify security if they need assistance, but gives no instruction about notifying guards whenever they leave.
questions.evidence: Notify security if assistance is needed.

parts.title: Passage 2 · What Is Happening to Our Planet?
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: 'Vanished' means disappeared, rather than merely changed or decreased.
questions.evidence: known species of birds and mammals have vanished

questions.explanation: Inhabitants are the living things that live in a particular place, here the rainforests.
questions.evidence: The Earth's rainforests are being destroyed, along with their inhabitants.

questions.explanation: 'Startling' means very surprising or shocking.
questions.evidence: startling warnings and predictions

questions.explanation: To urge someone to act is to strongly encourage them. It does not necessarily mean force them.
questions.evidence: urged the government to take immediate action

questions.explanation: 'Bleaker' means less hopeful or more discouraging about the future.
questions.evidence: a global report now would be even bleaker

questions.explanation: The opening paragraph links industries' growing use of natural resources with the disappearance of animal species.
questions.evidence: Industries use more and more of the Earth's natural resources.

questions.explanation: The passage identifies changes in the ozone layer and climate as threats to animals.
questions.evidence: Changes in the planet's ozone layer and in its climate threaten all animals.

questions.explanation: The study was carried out by several government departments under Barney's direction.
questions.evidence: at the direction of Dr. Gerald Barney

questions.explanation: The report predicted more human hardship and gave starvation as its example.
questions.evidence: more starvation, for example

questions.explanation: The first paragraph connects population growth and the use of resources with the disappearance of birds and mammals.
questions.evidence: The ever-increasing human population needs more space.

questions.explanation: Carter asked what would happen if the trends continued. Asking this conditional question does not state that he believed they definitely would continue.
questions.evidence: what ... would our planet be like in the year 2000 if present trends continue?

questions.explanation: The report gives a range from half a million to two million, not more than two million.
questions.evidence: between half a million and 2 million species

questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had been elected' means the election had already happened by the time the study was finished.
questions.evidence: by the time the study was completed, Ronald Reagan had been elected president

questions.explanation: The passage states that the administration ignored the report, but does not explicitly give its opinion about whether the report was necessary.
questions.evidence: his administration ignored the report

questions.explanation: The environmentalists worry about whether destruction can be stopped before it is too late. This presents acting too late as a possibility.
questions.evidence: wonder if we can stop the destruction of our planet before it is too late

questions.explanation: Their final question argues that humans should see themselves as guests rather than masters of the planet.
questions.evidence: they are not meant to be masters of the Earth, only one of its guests

parts.title: Passage 1 · What Is Stress?
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: A school principal is the headmaster or head of the school.
questions.evidence: the principal's office

questions.explanation: 'Bothersome' means annoying or causing trouble.
questions.evidence: bothersome noises

questions.explanation: To appraise something is to judge or assess it. The passage supplies this definition directly.
questions.evidence: appraise, or judge, circumstances

questions.explanation: 'Vary' means differ or change between people, not physically move or begin.
questions.evidence: vary from one person to another

questions.explanation: The opening paragraph says scientists find the concept of stress difficult to define.
questions.evidence: for scientists who study stress, it has been surprisingly hard to define

questions.explanation: The physical reactions listed occur when someone is in a stressful situation. The three-word phrase fits the summary.
questions.evidence: when you are placed in a stressful situation

questions.explanation: Stressors are the events or situations producing stress, as defined in the third paragraph.
questions.evidence: stressors: events or situations that produce stress

questions.explanation: The passage makes clear that even positive or pleasant events can cause stress.
questions.evidence: Even pleasant events can be stressors.

questions.explanation: Planning a party is the pleasant event paired with starting a new job in the passage.
questions.evidence: Planning a party or starting a new job

questions.explanation: The writer says knowledge of the feelings does not explain stress or identify its cause.
questions.evidence: nor does it tell us what causes it

questions.explanation: No comparison is made between the likelihood of stress from noise and from poor test results. They are simply listed as examples.
questions.evidence: A deadline, a poor test performance, or bothersome noises ... may be thought of as stressors.

questions.explanation: Both positive and negative events can cause stress, but the text does not establish that negative events generally cause more.
questions.evidence: Stress ... can be caused by both negative and positive events.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly calls the positive or negative interpretation a matter of personal choice in some cases.
questions.evidence: in some ways, a matter of personal choice

questions.explanation: An event becomes stressful according to the person's appraisal or interpretation of it.
questions.evidence: it is the way people interpret an event that makes it stressful or not stressful

questions.explanation: The writer specifically says circumstances that do not threaten or challenge us are not stressful.
questions.evidence: Those that do not threaten or challenge us are not stressful.

questions.explanation: Something stressful at one time may not be stressful at another time. Its status as a stressor can therefore change.
questions.evidence: the things that cause us stress today may not cause us stress at another time

parts.title: Passage 2 · Hot Days, Hot Nights
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: To delay is to put something off until later.
questions.evidence: an excuse for delaying action

questions.explanation: To shift is to move from one position or place to another.
questions.evidence: shifted north across the border

questions.explanation: 'Mild' describes something gentle or not severe.
questions.evidence: milder climates

questions.explanation: A drastic change is strong, sudden or extreme, fitting the exercise's definition.
questions.evidence: could be so drastic that many of the benefits would be lost

questions.explanation: To ban something is to forbid it.
questions.evidence: the use of CFCs ... has been banned

questions.explanation: To eliminate something is to get rid of it completely.
questions.evidence: we can't hope to eliminate it completely

questions.explanation: Paragraph A gives detailed predictions of hotter days and nights in Dallas, matching 'Warmer summer in Dallas'.
questions.evidence: in Dallas, a doubled level of carbon dioxide would increase the number of days

questions.explanation: Paragraph B focuses on possible harmful effects, including melting glaciers, rising seas, droughts and hurricanes.
questions.evidence: They also predict great droughts and hurricanes.

questions.explanation: Paragraph C introduces the view that changes could bring benefits, with Canadian farming as the example.
questions.evidence: the changes will be much more gradual, even beneficial

questions.explanation: Paragraph D warns that rapid, drastic change could cancel the benefits and create environmental refugees.
questions.evidence: many of the benefits would be lost

questions.explanation: Paragraph E introduces action already taken and gives the CFC ban as an important step.
questions.evidence: Some steps have already been taken.

questions.explanation: Paragraph F explains the suggested benefits of burning methane and using landfill gas for heating.
questions.evidence: Another strategy is to burn as much methane as possible.

questions.explanation: The passage predicts an increase from nineteen to seventy-eight Dallas days above 100 degrees.
questions.evidence: from nineteen to seventy-eight

questions.explanation: The four current nights refer to those when temperatures do not fall below 80 degrees. The statement reverses the condition.
questions.evidence: the temperature wouldn't fall below 80 degrees at night

questions.explanation: The passage says no one is certain about the speed or size of the rise, contradicting certainty among some scientists.
questions.evidence: no one is certain how fast and how much temperatures will rise

questions.explanation: The text says uncertainty gives policymakers an excuse to delay action. It does not state that they have no interest at all in acting.
questions.evidence: This gives policymakers an excuse for delaying action.

questions.explanation: Paragraph C explicitly presents some scientists' view that the changes could be beneficial.
questions.evidence: Other scientists think the changes will be much more gradual, even beneficial.

questions.explanation: Paragraph E directly links humanity's contribution to many basic activities.
questions.evidence: Humanity's contribution to the greenhouse effect comes from so many basic activities.

questions.explanation: According to the passage, converting methane to carbon dioxide is worthwhile because methane traps more heat. The strategy is presented as helpful rather than worsening the effect.
questions.evidence: methane traps twenty times as much heat as CO2, the net result is worthwhile

questions.explanation: The text reports that landfill gas heats homes in some places, but does not say people prefer methane to other fuels.
questions.evidence: It is being used to heat thousands of homes.

parts.title: Passage 1 · A Health Education Booklet
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: 'Rough' means uneven, rather than soft or high.
questions.evidence: a hard or rough surface

questions.explanation: For a person's body, 'stiff' describes difficulty moving freely. 'Difficult to bend' expresses a closely related physical meaning and is also accepted here.
questions.evidence: the child may be stiff the next day

questions.explanation: A Casualty Department treats people after accidents or injuries. It is not a place only for deaths or operations.
questions.evidence: taken to a hospital Casualty Department

questions.explanation: To relieve pain is to lessen or reduce it, rather than necessarily cure its cause.
questions.evidence: to relieve the pain

questions.explanation: The grazes section says the injury should be left uncovered so air can reach it.
questions.evidence: After cleaning, leave the graze uncovered.

questions.explanation: In the insect-bites section, calamine lotion is named as a way to relieve itching.
questions.evidence: The itching can be relieved by calamine lotion.

questions.explanation: The cuts section describes applying pressure to stop bleeding.
questions.evidence: Bleeding can usually be stopped by applying pressure to the cut.

questions.explanation: The bruises section mentions a cold compress made from material soaked in water.
questions.evidence: A cold compress may ease a bad bruise if applied at once.

questions.explanation: For a deep cut whose edges cannot be brought together with a dressing, the booklet says to consult a doctor or nurse.
questions.evidence: If the cut is deep and the edges cannot be pulled together with a dressing, consult the doctor.

questions.explanation: Redness of the skin is the symptom described under burns and scalds.
questions.evidence: Minor burns and scalds cause redness of the skin.

questions.explanation: The discussion of head bruises connects remembering the accident with a lower likelihood of serious injury.
questions.evidence: can remember the accident, it is unlikely that serious injury has resulted

questions.explanation: The cuts paragraph puts stopping the bleeding before inspecting the cut.
questions.evidence: The cut can then be carefully inspected.

questions.explanation: For severe bruising, the booklet gives a rest period of 24–48 hours, or one to two days.
questions.evidence: Severe bruising can be treated by rest for 24 to 48 hours.

questions.explanation: According to the cuts paragraph, applying pressure is the action associated with stopping bleeding.
questions.evidence: by applying pressure to the cut

questions.explanation: The passage says free bleeding normally washes germs away.
questions.evidence: any germs will normally have been washed away by the blood

questions.explanation: The grazes section says a dressing may stick to the injury or make it infected.
questions.evidence: It is not a good idea to apply a dressing.

questions.explanation: The text explicitly says bruises are very common in children.
questions.evidence: Bruises are very common in children.

questions.explanation: The booklet says the child may feel stiff on the day after the fall.
questions.evidence: the child may be stiff the next day

questions.explanation: The passage gives lying in bed as the easiest way to keep a badly bruised leg raised.
questions.evidence: Lying in bed is the easiest way to do this.

questions.explanation: The question refers to the sentence linking head bruises with anxiety. Its intended location is the head.
questions.evidence: Bruises on the head may cause anxiety.

parts.title: Passage 2 · Global Warming
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: To release a gas means emit it or let it out.
questions.evidence: release carbon into the air

questions.explanation: 'Trapped' means caught or prevented from escaping.
questions.evidence: heat ... to remain trapped

questions.explanation: To contribute to an effect is to help bring it about, without necessarily being its main cause.
questions.evidence: you contribute to the greenhouse effect

questions.explanation: To exhale means breathe out. It is the opposite of breathe in.
questions.evidence: human beings exhale it every time they breathe

questions.explanation: 'Exclusively' means only. The sentence says carbon dioxide is not the only gas involved.
questions.evidence: not exclusively responsible

questions.explanation: The passage directly states a fifty-fold increase in industrial production over the previous century.
questions.evidence: industrial production has increased by fifty times

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, so C completes this key point.
questions.evidence: When fossil fuels are burned, they release carbon into the air in the form of carbon dioxide.

questions.explanation: The text explains carbon dioxide's effect on the Earth's surface temperature by comparing temperatures with and without it.
questions.evidence: the average surface temperature on Earth would be 0 degrees Fahrenheit, instead of 59

questions.explanation: The scientists' measurements and projections describe rising carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere.
questions.evidence: The current reading is near 360 parts per million.

questions.explanation: The opening paragraph says hardly anyone knows what the catchphrases mean or how they relate to one another.
questions.evidence: hardly anyone knows what these terms really mean

questions.explanation: Four fifths of the growth came since 1950, so most came after that date rather than before it.
questions.evidence: Four fifths of that growth has come since 1950.

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says carbon dioxide allows heat that would escape to stay trapped.
questions.evidence: Carbon dioxide allows heat ... to remain trapped.

questions.explanation: Both activities are listed, but the passage does not compare how much fuel they use.
questions.evidence: take a hot shower, or make toast

questions.explanation: The passage links the use of energy, including electricity, to the greenhouse effect.
questions.evidence: It is a by-product of the use of energy — electricity, gasoline, or oil.

questions.explanation: The projected level is at least 560 parts per million, compared with about 280 before the Industrial Revolution. The intended comparison is a doubling of that earlier level.
questions.evidence: the carbon dioxide level should reach at least 560 parts per million

questions.explanation: Other greenhouse gases are listed, but their effects are not ranked against carbon dioxide's effects.
questions.evidence: Other greenhouse gases include chlorofluorocarbons, nitrogen oxides and methane.

parts.title: Passage 1 · University of Western Sydney Macarthur
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: A metropolitan area includes a city and its surrounding suburbs.
questions.evidence: the Sydney metropolitan area

questions.explanation: Here faculties are the university's branches of learning, such as Business and Law.
questions.evidence: courses are taught through its six faculties

questions.explanation: 'Annual' means happening or charged every year.
questions.evidence: Fees indicated are annual.

questions.explanation: Equivalent qualifications are equal or comparable in value to the stated qualifications.
questions.evidence: or equivalent qualifications

questions.explanation: Mature students are adults rather than necessarily teenagers or retired people.
questions.evidence: Mature age students

questions.explanation: Bankstown is 25 minutes from the business district by train, compared with 50 minutes for Campbelltown.
questions.evidence: it is 25 minutes by train from the Sydney Central Business District

questions.explanation: The annual fees explicitly exclude fees for English courses.
questions.evidence: except for English course fees

questions.explanation: The contact address for the Office of International Programmes is in Campbelltown.
questions.evidence: Campbelltown NSW 2560

questions.explanation: Either named examination answers the question, which asks for one English exam.
questions.evidence: 570 in TOEFL or 6.0 in IELTS

questions.explanation: The passage places Bankstown within Sydney's metropolitan area, rather than presenting it as a separate town outside that area.
questions.evidence: Bankstown is a city within the Sydney metropolitan area.

questions.explanation: The passage gives enrolment figures for 2008 but does not provide the previous year's figures for comparison.
questions.evidence: Total enrolment in 2008 exceeded 27,000.

questions.explanation: The faculty list explicitly puts Education & Languages mainly at Bankstown.
questions.evidence: Education & Languages (mainly at Bankstown)

questions.explanation: The directory says all the listed courses are full-time, not partly part-time.
questions.evidence: All courses are full-time.

questions.explanation: The passage says Summer Term subjects incur extra fees, so their charges are not part of the indicated annual amount.
questions.evidence: Extra fees are charged for ... attempting subjects in Summer Term.

questions.explanation: Mature students may be considered through other qualifications or work experience even if they lack the usual secondary-school qualification.
questions.evidence: will still be considered on the basis of other qualifications and/or work experience

questions.explanation: The alternative evidence is study through English as the language of instruction, subject to university approval. Merely having good English courses is a different condition.
questions.evidence: a school or university which has English as the language of instruction

questions.explanation: All the dates are explicitly subject to final confirmation, so they have not been finally confirmed.
questions.evidence: All dates are subject to final confirmation.

parts.title: Passage 2 · Our Diet Matters
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: To inherit is to receive something from one's parents or ancestors.
questions.evidence: the genes you inherit from your parents

questions.explanation: Upbringing means the training and care received while growing up.
questions.evidence: Your upbringing shapes some basic attitudes to food.

questions.explanation: To nibble means eat in small bites.
questions.evidence: nibble between meals

questions.explanation: To alter something means change it or make it different.
questions.evidence: these can alter the balance between food and fitness

questions.explanation: Ancestors are the people from whom someone is descended. The text uses the plural form.
questions.evidence: our ancestors were used to eating

questions.explanation: Disorder means lack of order; in this passage the plural refers to problems affecting the digestive system.
questions.evidence: various disorders of the digestive system

questions.explanation: The adjective 'digestive' relates to digesting food.
questions.evidence: the digestive system

questions.explanation: 'Slim' means attractively thin; here it is used as a verb meaning become thinner.
questions.evidence: help you to slim

questions.explanation: Section I warns that eating too much of some things and too little of others can harm health.
questions.evidence: your health will suffer

questions.explanation: Section II explains differences between people, including genes, upbringing, lifestyle, age and sex.
questions.evidence: everybody's different

questions.explanation: Section III discusses all three groups—proteins, vitamins and minerals—so F covers the whole section, unlike the heading about vitamin pills alone.
questions.evidence: proteins, vitamins or minerals

questions.explanation: Section IV explains that energy eaten beyond the body's use is stored as fat.
questions.evidence: the extra energy is stored as body fat

questions.explanation: Section V focuses on fibre, the modern diet's shortage of it and the reasons to eat more of it.
questions.evidence: the sort of food we eat today contains very little fibre

questions.explanation: Section II identifies inherited genes, exercise and attitudes to food as influences. The paragraph does not identify vitamin pills or excessive worries as the requested factors.
questions.evidence: the genes you inherit ... basic attitudes to food ... how much exercise you get

questions.explanation: The passage says weight gain is more likely with increasing age and especially for women. The older woman is therefore the intended comparison.
questions.evidence: more likely to put on weight as you get older, especially if you are a woman

questions.explanation: The text says energy intake should exactly balance energy used, contradicting the claim that it should be higher.
questions.evidence: should exactly balance the energy your body-machine burns up

questions.explanation: Section V contrasts the fibre-rich plant diet of ancestors with the much lower fibre content of the modern diet described.
questions.evidence: In comparison with our ancestors ... very little fibre.

questions.explanation: For a fairly varied diet, the passage says vitamin pills are generally unnecessary unless there is a special medical reason.
questions.evidence: Unless you have some special medical reason, it is a waste of time and money to take vitamin pills.

questions.explanation: The main body gives explanations about diet, metabolism, nutrients, energy and fibre. Its primary function is to inform the reader, although it also includes advice.
questions.evidence: What you eat and the way it affects your body depend very much on the kind of person you are.

parts.title: Passage 1 · All about Renting I
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: To refund money is to repay it to the person who paid it.
questions.evidence: the security deposit will be refunded

questions.explanation: To vacate an apartment is to move out of it.

parts.title: Passage 1 · How New York Became America's Largest City
parts.instructions: Follow the original instructions and word limits shown on the book pages. Choose the requested letters or write your answers.

questions.explanation: Routes are the paths or areas travelled along between places.
questions.evidence: trade routes from the ports to the central regions

questions.explanation: Freight means goods transported from one place to another.
questions.evidence: moving heavy freight very far

questions.explanation: A strip is a long, narrow piece of something.
questions.evidence: a long strip of low land

questions.explanation: Regions are areas of a country.
questions.evidence: the central regions of the country

questions.explanation: 'Consequently' introduces a result, so it means 'as a result'.
questions.evidence: Exports from New York were greater than imports. Consequently ...

questions.explanation: Section 1 introduces geography, history and economics as the three factors explaining the city's growth.
questions.evidence: geography, history, and economics

questions.explanation: Section 2 describes seaports as places where goods enter and leave the country.
questions.evidence: around seaports

questions.explanation: Section 3 says a favourable location alone does not explain the growth of a great industrial city.
questions.evidence: needed more than their geographical location

questions.explanation: Section 5 follows the canal's completion with the extension of the inland water transport network.
questions.evidence: a great inland shipping system

questions.explanation: Section 6 deals with the arrival of the railroads and their effect on transport.
questions.evidence: The coming of the railroads

questions.explanation: Section 7 explains why shipping companies could offer cheap passenger journeys from Europe.
questions.evidence: Passengers could come from Europe very cheaply

questions.explanation: Section 8 focuses on New York as the major arrival port for people from Europe.
questions.evidence: the greatest port for receiving people from European countries

questions.explanation: Section 3 explicitly rejects the idea that geographical location by itself made cities such as New York great industrial centres.
questions.evidence: needed more than their geographical location

questions.explanation: The passage says people had already moved west by about 1815, then describes wagons used to carry freight. It does not specify how those people travelled.
questions.evidence: many Americans ... had already moved toward the west ... moving heavy freight

questions.explanation: A canal seemed the best solution in New York State, but the text does not report agreement by every American.
questions.evidence: In New York State, a canal seemed the best solution

questions.explanation: The canal followed the low land from the eastern end of Lake Erie to the Hudson River.
questions.evidence: From the eastern end of Lake Erie ... to the Hudson River ... Here the Erie Canal was constructed.

questions.explanation: Freight costs fell immediately to about one tenth of their former level.
questions.evidence: The canal produced an immediate effect. Freight costs were cut to about one tenth

questions.explanation: The arrival of railroads made canal shipping less important.
questions.evidence: The coming of the railroads made canal shipping less important

questions.explanation: The final section directly credits the newcomers' labour with helping the city become great.
questions.evidence: Their labour helped the city become great.
